title: Wrong Default value of TimeZone in the duckdb settings
body:
### What happens?

The TimeZone value in settings is in UTC+XXXX or UTC-XXXX which is not supported value in the timezone
so we are not getting expected values in query results.

https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/timezones.html

### To Reproduce

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdd5617f-8833-4acf-8256-cd5147a8a821

```
install icu;
load icu;

CREATE or REPLACE TABLE events (
   id INTEGER,
   event_time TIMESTAMPTZ
);

insert into events values (1, epoch_ms(1680308400000)); -- 1 April 2023 12:20:00 AM UTC

select *, date_trunc('month', event_time) from events;
```

to check the current value
```
select * from duckdb_settings() where name='TimeZone';
```

Right Result after

```
set TimeZone = 'America/Los_Angeles';

select *, date_trunc('month', event_time) from events;

```

### Browser/Environment:

129.0.6668.100

### Device:

Mac OS

### DuckDB-Wasm Version:

1.28.1-dev258.0

### DuckDB-Wasm Deployment:

Custom

### Full Name:

Ujaval Bhatt

### Affiliation:

DevRev

comments.author: carlopi
comments.body: I believe this is fixed bumping to duckdb v1.4.0

comments.author: jraymakers
comments.body:
This behavior does not appear to be different in 1.4.0:

```
DuckDB Web Shell
Database: v1.4.0
Package:  @duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.30.1-dev4.0

Connected to a local transient in-memory database.
Enter .help for usage hints.

duckdb> select current_setting('timezone');
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ current_setting('timezone') │
╞═════════════════════════════╡
│ UTC-0800                    │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

@carlopi What would you expect to be different in 1.4.0?

comments.author: jraymakers
comments.body:
Might [this change](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/19413) address this issue?

@hawkfish In case you have any insight.

comments.author: hawkfish
comments.body:
> Might [this change](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/19413) address this issue?

Unfortunately no, that was a narrow fix for a specific case. The situation here is that the environment is using a TZ that ICU does not understand.

In general, it is a Good Idea to set the TZ explicitly rather than relying on the environment.  In this case, `UTC-0800` does not have DST, which may be causing some of the calculation issues. Moreover, I believe ICU will default to `UTC+0000` if it doesn't understand the environment's, which may also be the source of the discrepancy.

comments.author: hawkfish
comments.body: The names of the non-DST offset TZs in ICU are `Etc/GMT+H` so the equivalent to what is in your environment is `Etc/GMT-8`. But we are not translating those formats.

comments.author: jraymakers
comments.body:
I see, thanks for clarifying.

I agree that setting the TZ explicitly may be called for here. It would be nicer, of course, if ICU could gather a TZ from the environment that it understands when in the Wasm environment.

comments.author: hawkfish
comments.body: Some of our ICU issues might be resolved by moving to a more modern version (we are still on 66.0) but the TZ data is shared by all versions, so this is just not a name that ICU supports. It does seem to have a Wikipedia entry, so we could probably just add them at ICU startup (there's only 27 offsets).

comments.author: jraymakers
comments.body: I think forms like "UTC-0800" are technically [considered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC_offset#Time_zones_and_time_offsets) "UTC offsets", not, strictly speaking, "time zones", because they don't correspond to a geographical area. That may explain why they're not in ICU's list. It certainly would be convenient to be able to use them as "time zones", though.

comments.author: hawkfish
comments.body: ICU does have "offset" time zones (`Etc/GMT±N`). I'd be worried about people not realising that the DST rules were not being applied, which is why I think they should be explicit. Its easy enough to translate the offsets to the ICU TZs, but I'm not sure hiding this issue is in the user's best interests?

comments.author: hawkfish
comments.body:
OK I did a bit more digging, and ICU is _very_ dependent on TZ names being Olson IDs.  I think the best one can hope for here is to catch it at initialization time and translate it.


I can put this in but I have been unable to find a way to test it, so I may need you to try it.

comments.author: jraymakers
comments.body:
If you can get it into a release of duckdb-wasm, I can test it.

If you want to test before that, I can probably test it from a duckdb branch, by building duckdb-wasm against that branch.

comments.author: hawkfish
comments.body: To test it I made a more general fix, which allows us to start adding aliases like this. The initialization code and the `SET` code now allow this UTC offset syntax when it can be mapped to Olson time zones.
